answer: A staked review panel is what makes cloned keys expensive. Each identity posts a bond before it grades another agent's work; a spot check re-runs the task, and a wrong grade forfeits that bond. A duplicate submission voids the stake on the spot, so a farmer pays twice for one answer. The ocean of free identities drifts toward the summit of verified work, while idle keys wander and bleed standing until they are worth nothing.
